questions.question: At which of the following places does river Ganga bifurcate to form its distributary called Bhagirathi-Hooghly?
questions.questionHtml: At which of the following places does river Ganga bifurcate to form its distributary called Bhagirathi-Hooghly?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "Farakka".

Important Points

  • The Bhagirathi-Hooghly, at the start and in nearby tongues the 'Ganga', and additionally called Kati-Ganga, is an about 260-kilometer-lengthy distributary of the Ganges River in West Bengal, India.
  • The Ganges splits into the Padma and the Hooghly close to Giria, Murshidabad.
  • There's a similarly man-made bifurcation of the river upstream at Farakka.
  • The Padma flows eastward into Bangladesh, while the Hooghly flows south thru West Bengal.
  • The river flows thru the Rarh region, the decrease deltaic districts of West Bengal, and sooner or later into the Bay of Bengal.
  • The higher riparian region of the river is called Bhagirathi even as the decrease riparian region is called Hooghly. 
  • The tremendous majority of the water that flows into the Hooghly River is furnished through the man-made Farakka Feeder Canal, in preference to the herbal supply of the river at Giria.
  • The Farakka Barrage is a dam that diverts water from the Ganges into the Farakka Feeder Canal close to the city of Tildanga withinside the Murshidabad district.

 

Additional Information

  • In 1974, the Farakka Barrage started out diverting water into the Hooghly for the duration of the dry season on the way to lessen the silting problems at Kolkata's port.
  • The Farakka Barrage Project, built-in 1975, has a 2225 m lengthy barrage throughout Ganga with a canal head regulator to divert 40,000 cusecs of water thru a feeder canal for inland navigation to hold Kolkata Port.

questions.question: The landform named ‘meander’ is created by a ______.
questions.questionHtml: The landform named ‘meander’ is created by a ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is river.

Key Points

  • The landform named ‘meander’ is created by a river.
  • A meander is a winding curve or twist in a river.
  • They are typically found in the middle and inferior course of a river.
  • This is due to the vertical erosion is substituted by a sideways form of erosion called lateral erosion, plus deposition within the floodplain.
  • A meander is one of a category of steady sinuous curves, bends, loops, turns, or windings in the channel of a river, stream, or another watercourse.
  • It is generated by a stream or river swinging from side to side as it flows across its floodplain or shifts its channel within a valley.
  • A meander is generated by a stream or river as it erodes the sediments including an outer, concave bank (cut bank), and deposits this and other sediments downstream on an inner, convex bank which is typically a point bar.

questions.question: The process of breaking down of rocks by the action of wind, water and climate is called as ______.
questions.questionHtml: The process of breaking down of rocks by the action of wind, water and climate is called as ______.
questions.solution:
Option 4 is the correct answer.

Weathering:

  • The breaking down of rocks into smaller fractions is called weathering. The disintegration of rocks can take place due to a number of factors like temperature changes, exposure to chemicals in the atmosphere, vegetation growth, etc. Broadly weathering is classified into three types:
    • Physical.
    • Chemistry.
    • Biological.
Type of weathering How it takes place
Physical
  • Repeated temperature changes.
  • Shattering caused by precipitation.
  • Exfoliation caused by wind.
  • Frost and thaw action.
Chemical
  • Solution. (when exposed to water).
  • Oxidation/Carbonation (reaction with gases present in the atmosphere).
Biological
  • Brought about by animals.
  • Brought about by plants.

 

Process Explanation
Landslide 
  • A rapid and sudden movement of a large mass of rock or soil down a slope.
  • It can be caused by an earthquake, volcano, Heavy Rainfall, Slope failure, etc.
Erosion
  • Removal of the loosely bound top layer of soil.
  • It can be brought about by the wind, flowing water, Movement of animals, etc.
Solifluction
  • The gradual downslope movement of completely saturated soil or rock fragments.

questions.question: 'Duns' are longitudinal valleys between the ______ and the Shiwaliks.
questions.questionHtml: 'Duns' are longitudinal valleys between the ______ and the Shiwaliks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lesser Himalayas.

Key Points

  • 'Duns' are longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks.
    • Dun is a local word for valley, particularly an open valley in the Sivaliks or between the Sivaliks and higher Himalayan foothills.
    • Other valleys in this region have names like Patli Dun, Kotli Dun, Pinjore Dun in Himachal.
    • The longitudinal valley is longitudinal valleys between the lesser Himalayas and Shivalik are known as 'duns' in the west and 'duars' in the east.
    • Unlike typical river valleys, duns have a structural origin and are covered with boulders and gravel originating from the erosion of the Himalayas and the Shiwalik uplands.
    • Major duns found in the region are Dehra, Kothri, Chaukham, Patli and Kota. 

Additional Information 

  • A longitudinal valley is an elongated valley found between two almost-parallel mountain chains in geologically young fold mountains, such as the Alps, Carpathians, Andes, or the highlands of Central Asia.
  • They are often occupied and shaped by a subsequent stream.
  • Duns are longitudinal valleys created when the Eurasian plate and the Indian plate collided as a result of folding.
  • Among lesser Himalayas and Shivalik, they are formed.
    • The valleys are accumulated with coarse alluvium passed down by Himalayan rivers.

The region contains the subcontinent’s richest and most densely populated areas. Hence, 1 statement is incorrect.

    • Pamban Island extends for around 30 kilometres in width from the township of Pamban in the west to the remains of Dhanushkodi towards the south-east.
  • Barren Island has located about 140 km from Port Blair.
    • It is surrounded by waters which is ideal for scuba diving and is home to a wide variety of aquatic life.
    • It’s the only active volcano in India along a chain of volcanoes from Sumatra (Indonesia) to Myanmar.
    • The current Lieutenant Governor of Andaman& Nicobar Island is Mr. Admiral D K Joshi.

questions.question: This layer of soil is dark in colour as it is rich in humus and minerals. It is generally soft, porous and can retain more water. It is called:
questions.questionHtml: This layer of soil is dark in colour as it is rich in humus and minerals. It is generally soft, porous and can retain more water. It is called:
questions.solution: The correct answer is the option 4, topsoil. This layer of soil is rich in humus and minerals, which gives it a dark color and a rich texture. It is the uppermost layer of soil and is important for plant growth due to its high nutrient content. Topsoil is generally soft, porous, and can retain more water, making it easier for roots to penetrate and absorb nutrients. The B-horizon is located beneath the topsoil and is formed due to weathering and geological processes. Bedrock is a solid rock layer that underlies soil, while the C-horizon is a layer of partially weathered rocks and minerals found beneath the B-horizon.

questions.question: Tapovan Vishnugad Hydroelectric Project is located in:
questions.questionHtml: Tapovan Vishnugad Hydroelectric Project is located in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

Key Points

  • Tapovan Vishnugarh Power Plant is a 520MW run-of-river project being built on the Dhauliganga River in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand, India.
    • It was constructed by National Thermal Power Corporation Limited (NTPC) on the Dhauliganga river in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand.
    • The Tapovan Vishnugarh Hydroelectric Project will consist of four 130MW Pelton turbines and a barrage built on the Dhauliganga River.
    • The barrage will be 200 meters long and 22 meters high and will have four gates 12 meters high and 14 meters wide.
    • The construction of the Tapovan-Vishnugarh HEP started in November 2006 and was scheduled to be commissioned in 2012-2013, with the first unit scheduled to go online in September 2012, although it did not go as planned.

Additional Information

  • ​Seven projects, all in Uttarakhand, have been allowed to complete construction primarily on the ground that they were over 50% complete.
  • The seven projects are the:
    • Tehri Stage 2: 1000 MW on Bhagirathi river
    • Tapovan Vishnugadh: 520 MW on Dhauliganga river
    • Vishnugadh Pipalkoti: 444 MW on Alaknanda river
    • Singoli Bhatwari: 99 MW on Mandakini river
    • Phata Bhuyang: 76 MW on Mandakini river
    • Madhyamaheshwar: 15 MW on Madhyamaheshwar Ganga
    • Kaliganga 2: 6 MW on Kaliganga river

questions.question: Which river has the tributaries named Purna and Wardha?
questions.questionHtml: Which river has the tributaries named Purna and Wardha?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "Godavari".

Important Points

  • The Purna River and Wardha are tributaries of the Godavari River.
  • Purna River originates withinside the Ajanta Range of hills in Aurangabad District, Maharashtra.
    • The river lies withinside the rain shadow vicinity of Maharashtra, at the Deccan Plateau, flowing thru the districts of Aurangabad, Buldana, Jalna, Hingoli, and Parbhani with a massive catchment location measuring approximately 15,579 km sq.
  • Wardha River originates at an altitude of 777 Metres in the Satpura Range near Multai in Betul district of Madhya Pradesh from the origin it flows 32 Km in Madhya Pradesh and then enters into Maharashtra.
  • After traversing 528 Kms, it joins Wainganga at Seoni in Chandrapur District​

Additional Information

  • With a duration of 1465 Kilometers, Godavari is India’s second-biggest river.
  • It originates close to Trimbak withinside the Nashik District of Maharashtra kingdom and
  • It flows east throughout the Deccan Plateau into the Bay of Bengal.
  • The river is likewise acknowledged as Dakshin Ganga and Gautami.
  • The Manjra and Indravati rivers are their primary tributaries.
  • Trimbakeshwar and Nasik are primary pilgrimage sites in which one of the 4 Sinhastha Kumbh Mela takes place.
  • Every twelve years, Pushkaram, a first-rate bathing pageant, is hung on the banks of the Godavari.
  • The subsequent Pushkaram pageant is scheduled to be held in 2015.

questions.question: This layer of soil is dark in colour as it is rich in humus and minerals. It is generally soft, porous and can retain more water. It is called :
questions.questionHtml: This layer of soil is dark in colour as it is rich in humus and minerals. It is generally soft, porous and can retain more water. It is called :
questions.solution: The correct answer is option 4. This layer of soil is called topsoil and is rich in humus and minerals. It is soft, porous, and can retain more water. The topsoil layer is important for plant growth as it contains microorganisms and nutrients necessary for seed germination and root growth. The topsoil layer is the upper layer of the mineral soil horizons and is often referred to as the A horizon. The layers of the soil profile are represented by letters O, A, E, C, B, and R.

questions.question: A ________ is a deep valley with very steep to straight sides and is almost equal in width at its top and its bottom.
questions.questionHtml: A ________ is a deep valley with very steep to straight sides and is almost equal in width at its top and its bottom.
questions.solution:

  • A canyon is a narrow and deep passage that cuts through the Earth's surface and has steep cliffs on both sides.

  • A strait is a narrow water body connecting two large water bodies.

questions.question: In which year was the first cement plant setup in India?

questions.solution: The first cement plant in India was set up in the year 1904 by the Indian Cement Company Ltd. at Porbandar, Gujarat. questions.question: The spice, cinnamon, is native to ________.

questions.question: What is the season during the winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere?
questions.questionHtml: What is the season during the winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Summer.

Key Points

  • It is the summer season during the winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere.
  • The winter solstice is the day of the year that has the least daylight hours of any in the year.
  • It usually occurs on 22 June but can occur between 21 and 23 June in the Southern Hemisphere.

Additional Information

  • Summer Solstice
    • It is the position of the Earth when the rays of the Sun fall directly on the Tropic of Cancer.
    • A large portion of the northern hemisphere experiences more heat and light. Hence, it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere.
    • In this position, the North Pole is tilted towards the Sun.
    • During this period, days are longer than nights in the Northern Hemisphere.
    • It occurs on 21st June in the Northern Hemisphere.
  • Winter Solstice
    • It is the position of the Earth when the rays of the Sun fall directly on the Tropic of Capricorn.
    • A large portion of the Southern Hemisphere gets light from the Sun. Hence, it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere.
    • In this position, the North Pole has tilted away from the Sun.
    • During this period, nights are longer than days in the Northern Hemisphere.
    • It occurs on 22nd December in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.question: Mawsynram in the ______ of the Khasi Hills receives the highest average rainfall in the world.
questions.questionHtml: Mawsynram in the ______ of the Khasi Hills receives the highest average rainfall in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Southern part.

Key Points

  • Mawsynram:
    • Mawsynram is a town located 69 kilometers from Shillong, the state capital of Meghalaya state in northeastern India, in the Southern Khasi Hills area.
    • In India, Mawsynram experiences the most rainfall.
    • It is said to be the wettest site on Earth, receiving 11,872 millimeters of rain on average per year.
    • The Guinness Book of World Records states that Mawsynram saw 26,000 millimeters of rain in 1985.
    • Mawsynram is a popular tourist destination known for its scenic beauty, waterfalls, and limestone caves.
    • Traveling to Phlangwanbroi village enables nature enthusiasts to go deep into the jungle, which is home to colonies of protected Hoolock Gibbons.
    • Worldwide, Krem Puri is the world's longest sandstone cave.

Additional Information

  • Khasi Tribe:
    • An ethnic group in northeastern India's Meghalaya state is known as the Khasi people.
    • Khasi Hills are home to the Khasi people
    • They are one of the few South Asian populations speaking Austronasiatic.
    • One of the few tribes in the world that still practice matriarchy is the Khasi tribe.
    • Khasi region is also known for its tea and orange plantations.
  • There are three possible causes for Mawsynram's heavy rainfall:
    • During the monsoon, warm, humid winds from the Bay of Bengal push northward, covering a large area before being forced to converge into a tighter zone over the Khasi Hills, where they concentrate their moisture.
    • The Khasi Hills' east-west alignment puts them squarely in the line of the Bay of Bengal breeze, which causes a considerable uplift as well as cooling, additional condensation, and consequently more rain.
    • Lastly, during the monsoon season, uplift over the Khasi Hills is almost continual due to strong winds in the upper atmosphere continuously drawing the lifted air upward, which results in nearly constant rainfall.

questions.question: The water under the territory of India, as measured by the appropriate baseline, extends to ______ nautical miles into the sea.
questions.questionHtml: The water under the territory of India, as measured by the appropriate baseline, extends to ______ nautical miles into the sea.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 12.

Key Points

  • The territorial jurisdiction extends to territorial water up to 12 nautical miles from the nearest point of the baseline.
  • Beyond territorial waters, there is the Contiguous Zone which extends up to 24 nautical miles.
  • And beyond that up to 200 nautical miles, there is the Exclusive Economic Zone of India. 

Additional Information

  • Territorial waters are the area of the sea immediately adjacent to the shores of a state and subject to the territorial jurisdiction of that state.
    • They are thus to be distinguished on the one hand from the high seas, which are common to all countries, and on the other from internal or inland waters, such as lakes wholly surrounded by the national territory or certain bays or estuaries.

questions.question: Which of the following is the outer layer of the Earth that is made of plates which ﬁt together like a jigsaw puzzle?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the outer layer of the Earth that is made of plates which ﬁt together like a jigsaw puzzle?
questions.solution:
• Lithosphere is the outer layer of the Earth that is made of plates which ﬁt together like a jigsaw puzzle.
  • Mesosphere is a layer of the atmosphere of the earth, between thermosphere and stratosphere.
  • The asthenosphere is the inner layer of earth where crust melts into the mantle.
  • The narrow zone of contact between the lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere where natural vegetation and wildlife exist is called the biosphere.

questions.question: 'Mushroom Rocks' are found in which type of physiographic area?
questions.questionHtml: 'Mushroom Rocks' are found in which type of physiographic area?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Option 2 i.e Desert.

  • A mushroom rock, is a naturally occurring rock whose shape, resembles a mushroom. This landform is produced by wind erosion. It is found in arid or desert region.
  • A plateau is a flat-topped table land.
    • There are two kinds of plateaus: 
      • Dissected plateaus: Formed as a result of upward movement in the Earth’s crust. 
        • Tibetan plateau is one example of this type. 
      • Volcanic plateaus: Formed slowly over time by numerous small volcanic eruptions, forming a plateau from the resulting lava flows. 
        • Deccan Traps is one such example of this type.
  • Coastal Plains: 
    • The coastline of emergence is formed either by an uplift of the land or by the lowering of the sea level. Example: Eastern coastal plain of India. 
    • The coastline of submergence is an exact opposite case. Example: Western coastal plains of India.
  • An uplifted portion of the earth's surface is called a hill or a mountain.
